pl-l3d34c7-d1e115.summary: Notes that both servile and initial fear are called the beginning of wisdom in various Scripture passages, but for different reasons.
claims: Both fears are called the beginning of wisdom.

pl-l3d34c7-d1e121.summary: Explains that servile fear is the beginning of wisdom because it prepares a place for wisdom and leads to it, yet does not remain with it but goes out.
claims: Servile fear prepares for wisdom without remaining with it.

pl-l3d34c7-d1e128.summary: Explains that initial fear is the beginning of wisdom because it is in beginning wisdom: whoever begins to have it begins to have wisdom and charity. So both fears are sometimes called initial and sometimes servile, since initial fear has something of the servile, anguish at penalty, and something of the chaste, fear of offending and being separated.
claims: Whoever has initial fear begins to have wisdom and charity.
Initial fear has elements of servile and chaste fear.

pl-l3d34c7.summary: Notes that both servile and initial fear are called the beginning of wisdom in Scripture, for different reasons: servile fear prepares a place for wisdom and leads to it but does not remain; initial fear is in beginning wisdom, so that whoever begins to have it begins to have wisdom and charity. So both are sometimes called initial, and both sometimes servile, since initial fear has something of the servile, anguish at penalty, and something of the chaste, fear of offending and separation.
claims: Both servile and initial fear are called the beginning of wisdom, for different reasons.
Servile fear prepares for wisdom; initial fear coexists with beginning wisdom.
Initial fear shares features of servile and chaste fear.
